pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산 아래 조그만 마을이 있었어요. 마을 밖에는 나지막한 고개가 하나 있었지요. 사람들은 그 고개를 삼년고개라고 불렀어요. "저 고개에서 넘어지면 삼 년밖에 못 산대!" 하는 옛말이 전해 왔거든요. 그래서 다들 고개를 넘을 땐 발끝을 살피며 살금살금 걸었답니다. 마을에서는 할머니가 다듬잇돌에 무명천을 얹고 또닥또닥 두드리는 소리가 정답게 울렸지요.
pages.t: Long, long ago, there was a tiny village at the foot of a mountain. Just outside the village stood one low hill. People called it the Three-Year Hill. An old saying had been passed down: "If you fall on that hill, you'll only live three more years!" So whenever anyone crossed it, they watched their toes and tiptoed ever so carefully. Down in the village, a grandmother laid white cotton cloth on her laundry-beating stone and tapped it — tok-tok, tok-tok — a warm and friendly sound.

pages.ko: 마을에는 약초를 캐는 할아버지가 살았어요. 그날도 할아버지는 약초바구니를 지고 삼년고개를 넘었지요. 고갯마루 서낭당 돌탑 앞에서 돌 하나를 조심조심 얹었어요. "오늘도 넘어지지 않게 해 주세요." 그리고 살금, 살금, 아주 살금살금 걸었답니다.
pages.t: In that village lived an old man who gathered healing herbs. That day, too, he carried his herb basket on his back and crossed the Three-Year Hill. At the top of the hill, in front of the little stone tower at the village shrine, he set one more stone on the pile, ever so carefully. "Please keep me from falling today." And then he walked softly, softly, oh so very softly.

pages.ko: 그런데 해 질 무렵, 집으로 돌아오는 길이었어요. 툭! 돌부리에 발이 걸렸지 뭐예요. 데구루루— 데구루루— 할아버지는 고갯길을 한 바퀴 구르고 말았어요. 약초가 후두둑 쏟아지고, 엉덩이만 콩 찧었답니다.
pages.t: But at sundown, on his way back home — thump! His foot caught on a stone poking out of the path. Tumble, tumble, tumble-roll — the old man rolled all the way over. His herbs went flying everywhere, and he landed flat on his bottom.

pages.ko: 그제야 할아버지는 화들짝 놀랐어요. "아이고! 여기가… 삼년고개잖아!" 할아버지는 쏟은 약초도 그대로 두고, 털레털레 집으로 걸어 내려갔어요. 어깨가 축, 다리도 축 늘어졌지요.
pages.t: Only then did the old man gasp. "Oh no! This — this is the Three-Year Hill!" He left his spilled herbs right where they were and trudged all the way down home. His shoulders drooped, and his legs dragged too.

pages.ko: 집에 온 할아버지는 삿자리 위에 이불을 펴고 폭 드러누웠어요. "아이고, 아이고… 나는 이제 삼 년뿐이라네." 할머니가 기가 막혀 말했지요. "아이참, 죽이나 한 술 뜨세요!" 그래도 죽은 한 그릇 뚝딱 비웠답니다.
pages.t: When he got home, the old man spread his blanket on the reed mat and flopped straight down. "Oh dear, oh dear… I have only three years left now." His wife could hardly believe her ears. "Oh, come now — have a spoonful of porridge at least!" Yet he emptied the whole bowl in no time at all.

pages.ko: 소문을 들은 마을 사람들이 줄줄이 문병을 왔어요. "기운 내세요!" "약을 지어 볼까요?" 하지만 할아버지는 도리도리, 이불을 더 끌어 덮을 뿐이었지요. 그때 꾀돌이가 엿 한 봉지를 들고 방으로 쏙 들어왔답니다.
pages.t: The villagers heard the news and came to visit, one after another. "Cheer up!" "Shall we fetch you some medicine?" But the old man only shook his head, no, no, no, and pulled the blanket up higher. Just then a clever boy named Kkoedori slipped into the room with a little bag of chewy taffy.

pages.ko: 꾀돌이가 사연을 다 듣더니 무릎을 탁! 쳤어요. "할아버지, 그럼 한 번 더 구르면 되잖아요?" 할아버지는 벌떡 일어나 앉았어요. "뭐라고? 이 녀석이 지금 나를 놀리는 게냐!"
pages.t: When Kkoedori had heard the whole story, he slapped his knee — smack! "Grandfather, then all you have to do is roll one more time!" The old man sat bolt upright. "What did you say? Are you teasing me, you rascal?"

pages.ko: 꾀돌이는 손가락을 하나씩 꼽으며 말했어요. "한 번 구르면 삼 년! 두 번 구르면 육 년! 데굴데굴 구를수록 오래오래 산다네!" 할아버지의 두 눈이 번쩍 뜨였어요. "그… 그렇구나! 내가 왜 그 생각을 못 했지!"
pages.t: Kkoedori counted on his fingers, one by one. "Roll once, three years! Roll twice, six years! The more you roll and roll, the longer and longer you live!" The old man's eyes flew wide open. "That… that's right! Why didn't I think of that!"

pages.ko: 할아버지는 한달음에 삼년고개로 달려갔어요. 그러고는 풀밭에 몸을 동그랗게 말고 데굴데굴 굴렀지요! 마을 아이들이 손뼉을 치며 세어 주었어요. "삼 년! 육 년! 구 년! 십이 년!" "한 번 구르면 삼 년, 두 번 구르면 육 년! 데굴데굴 구를수록 오래오래 산다네!"
pages.t: The old man ran all the way to the Three-Year Hill without stopping once. Then he curled himself up round as a ball on the grass and rolled and rolled and rolled! The village children clapped their hands and counted for him. "Three years! Six years! Nine years! Twelve years!" "Roll once, three years! Roll twice, six years! The more you roll and roll, the longer and longer you live!"

pages.ko: 한참을 구르고 난 할아버지가 벌떡 일어섰어요. 어깨를 툭툭, 다리를 탈탈 털고 나니 몸이 어찌나 가뿐한지! "허허허! 이제 나는 백 년도 넘게 살겠구나!" 걱정은 어느새 저 멀리 날아가 버렸답니다.
pages.t: After rolling for a good long while, the old man sprang to his feet. He patted off his shoulders, shook out his legs — and oh, how light his whole body felt! "Ho ho ho! Now I shall live more than a hundred years!" His worry had already flown far, far away.

pages.ko: 그날부터 마을 사람들은 고개에만 오면 일부러 데굴데굴 굴렀어요. "한 번 구르면 삼 년! 두 번 구르면 육 년! 데굴데굴 구를수록 오래오래 산다네!" 사람들은 이제 그 고개를 만년고개라고 불렀지요. 할아버지는 엿을 나누어 주며 오래오래 껄껄 웃었답니다. 걱정도 뒤집어 보면 복이 된대요.
pages.t: From that day on, whenever the villagers came to the hill, they rolled down it on purpose. "Roll once, three years! Roll twice, six years! The more you roll and roll, the longer and longer you live!" Now people called it the Ten-Thousand-Year Hill. And the old man shared out his taffy and laughed and laughed for a long, long time. They say even a worry can turn into a blessing, if you flip it upside down.
